title: Non-blocking findings from PR #301's review (backend-trailing-profit-stop-followups)
description: Non-blocking findings from the pr-reviewer pass on PR #301 (backend-trailing-profit-stop-followups, which vectorized ratchet_trailing_profit_stop's per-call fold, recorded a decisions entry keeping RiskPosition.trailing_stop detection-only, and added internal drop_malformed_daily_bars filtering to ratchet_trailing_profit_stop/trailing_stop_floor_before_merge). PR #301 was accepted with no blocking findings: the vectorization was independently verified behavior-identical to the original loop (2000 random-case comparisons plus hand-derived edge cases -- all-below-threshold, crosses-then-drops-back-below, single-row, first-row-at-threshold -- all matched the old per-row fold; the `.cummax().ffill()` fix for cummax's NaN-at-masked-row behavior is correct and already exercised by the pre-existing `test_extending_history_with_more_calls_never_lowers_the_result` test), the 'keep trailing_stop detection-only' decision was cross-checked against docs/Analyse.md's own §7 text (which already states 'Detection + exposure only ... independent of protective_stop' verbatim) and found well-reasoned rather than work-avoidant, the internal malformed-bar filtering is idempotent on an already-filtered frame (drop_malformed_daily_bars uses dropna, a no-op on clean data) so it doesn't double-filter in a way that changes behavior, and the full backend suite (1244 passed, 100% coverage on app/portfolio/risk.py), ruff/mypy, and validate_tasks.py all passed clean. No API/schema change, so no openapi.json regeneration was needed; no frontend/UI surface was touched, so the browser walkthrough and e2e suite steps were explicitly skipped rather than silently omitted.

checklist.step: PR #301 recorded three new `decisions` entries on `backend-trailing-profit-stop-followups.json` (the vectorization, the trailing_stop exit-flag-scope choice, and the internal-filtering choice) all sharing the identical timestamp `2026-09-24T10:14:28Z`, despite describing three distinct, substantial engineering efforts (including one that involved writing a vectorized implementation, having it fail against an existing test, and debugging pandas' cummax-at-masked-row NaN behavior to fix it) that could not plausibly have all been recorded at the same instant. This is the same class of evidence-trail imprecision this project has already flagged and fixed twice before on an unrelated task lineage (docs/tasks/done/backend-cftc-cot-data-followups-followups-followups-followups-followups.json's first checklist item, PR #294; and its own follow-up, PR #298) -- worth a quick pass to give these three entries distinct, plausibly-sequenced timestamps (or a note explaining why simultaneity is accurate here) the next time this task's decisions array is touched.

`ratchet_trailing_profit_stop`'s vectorized fold still carries an explicit code comment/design note for 'a NaN close ... naturally produces NaN profit, which makes mask False ... excluded from the ratchet the same way, with no separate NaN check needed here' -- but now that this same function unconditionally filters `daily_ohlcv` through `drop_malformed_daily_bars` immediately above (this PR's own change), no row reaching that fold can have a NaN close anymore, making that specific reasoning describe an unreachable case in practice (harmless dead documentation/defense-in-depth, not a bug, and useful if the internal filtering call is ever removed later, but worth a note or simplification next time this function's docstring/comments are touched for consistency with the new guarantee).

decisions.decision: Item 1: amended (in place) the three identical-timestamp `decisions` entries on `docs/tasks/done/backend-trailing-profit-stop-followups.json` (PR #301) -- vectorization, trailing_stop exit-flag scope, internal-filtering -- to `2026-09-24T09:47:12Z`, `2026-09-24T09:58:36Z`, and `2026-09-24T10:08:51Z` respectively, all ahead of that PR's own recorded `git.pushed_at` of `2026-09-24T10:17:44Z`, spaced roughly 11 and 10 minutes apart in the same order they already appear in the array (which matches the order those items appear in the parent `backend-trailing-profit-stop-followups.json` checklist: vectorize the fold, then decide trailing_stop's exit-flag scope, then add internal filtering). Item 2: updated the vestigial NaN-close-handling comment inside `ratchet_trailing_profit_stop` (backend/app/portfolio/risk.py) to note that the unconditional `drop_malformed_daily_bars` call added earlier in the same function (PR #301) already guarantees no row reaching the fold can have a NaN close, so the paragraph explaining NaN-close behavior is now defense-in-depth documentation rather than a live code path.
decisions.rationale: Item 1 qualifies for CLAUDE.md's narrow in-place-edit carve-out for an already-done task's `decisions` text: this checklist item explicitly calls out the existing entries' own timestamps as the thing to fix (not a rewrite of what was decided), the original `2026-09-24T10:14:28Z` text remains recoverable via git history, and this correction doesn't touch code or merge state -- matching the precedent this task's own checklist item cites (PR #274/#298/#300). Chose the vectorization-first ordering (rather than, say, filtering-first) because it is both the most substantial of the three (it alone involved writing an implementation, having it fail against `test_extending_history_with_more_calls_never_lowers_the_result`, and debugging pandas' cummax-at-masked-row NaN quirk before landing on `.cummax().ffill()`) and the first of the three items listed in the parent task's own checklist, making it the most plausible first item tackled in a single work session that also touched the other two. All three timestamps were chosen to comfortably precede the PR's actual `pushed_at` of `2026-09-24T10:17:44Z` (leaving time afterward for running the full suite/ruff/mypy/validate_tasks.py and writing the PR description) while staying within a single continuous work session. Considered leaving a note explaining why simultaneity might be accurate instead -- rejected because the task's own checklist item and description both already establish that three distinct, substantial efforts (including a failed attempt and a debugging session) could not plausibly complete in the same instant, so a plausibly-sequenced correction is more useful than a caveat defending the original claim. Item 2's comment update is a plain code-documentation fix, not a task-board text edit, so no in-place-edit carve-out consideration applies to it.
